s: Which of the following amendment pairs is correctly matched?
o: 21st Amendment – Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali added
71st Amendment – Bodo, Santhali, Maithili and Dogri added
x: The 102nd Amendment gave NCBC constitutional status; the 21st added Sindhi, the 71st Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, and the 92nd Bodo, Santhali, Maithili and Dogri.

s: In the Governor changes of March 2026, R.N. Ravi was moved to which State?
x: R.N. Ravi went from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal; Jishnu Dev Varma went to Maharashtra, Shiv Pratap Shukla to Telangana and Kavinder Gupta to Himachal Pradesh.

s: Puducherry's legislature rests on Article 239A, inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 239A was inserted by the 14th Amendment and, with the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963, provides Puducherry's legislature; Article 239AA (69th Amendment) relates to Delhi.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in K. Lakshminarayanan v UoI (2019) concerning the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry?
o: The Lieutenant Governor must administer Puducherry without elected members
The Lieutenant Governor can act independently in all routine matters
The Lieutenant Governor can legislate on any State List subject
The Lieutenant Governor cannot act independently in routine matters
x: K. Lakshminarayanan v UoI (2019) held that the Puducherry Lieutenant Governor cannot act independently in routine matters. The other options reverse or add to that limitation.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Union Territories with legislatures is incorrect?
o: Puducherry’s legislature was created by law and is unicameral, with elected and nominated members.
Delhi’s legislature is provided for in the Constitution under Article 239AA, but it has no power over public order, police and land.
Jammu and Kashmir has the closest level of autonomy to a State among the three Union Territories with legislatures.
In Jammu and Kashmir, police and public order remain with the Lieutenant Governor, while Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature.
x: The incorrect statement is that Jammu and Kashmir has the closest level of autonomy to a State. Puducherry is the closest to a State, while Jammu and Kashmir has the least autonomy among the three. The statement about Delhi’s limited powers is correct.

s: Under the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee's proposal, the President would choose a Governor from how many names proposed by the State?
x: The State would propose three names, approved by an Assembly majority, and the President would pick one.

s: In the March 2026 Governor changes, Nand Kishore Yadav was appointed Governor of which State?
x: Nand Kishore Yadav became Governor of Nagaland; Syed Ata Hasnain went to Bihar, Shiv Pratap Shukla to Telangana and Jishnu Dev Varma to Maharashtra.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the development of the Hindi language?
x: Article 351 concerns the development of Hindi; Article 344 deals with the Official Language Commission and Committee.

s: What does Article 246(4) enable Parliament to do in relation to Union Territories?
o: Make regulations only for Andaman and Lakshadweep
Legislate on any subject, including subjects in the State List
Impose President's Rule only in Delhi
Appoint High Courts for every Union Territory
x: Article 246(4) enables Parliament to legislate on any subject, including a subject in the State List, for Union Territories. The other options describe different constitutional provisions or incorrectly restrict Parliament's power.

s: Article 239AB provides for President's Rule, similar to Article 356, in which Union Territory?
x: Article 239AB concerns Delhi, not Puducherry.

s: Under the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee's proposals, who would discharge the Governor's functions on an interim basis?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: The proposal names the Chief Justice of the High Court, not the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

s: The Justice Kurian Joseph Committee proposed deleting which Article, relating to the Governor's special address?
x: The committee proposed deletion of Article 176, along with a fixed five-year tenure via Articles 155 and 156.

s: The Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance, 2026 made which languages official alongside English?
x: The ordinance made Khasi and Garo official languages alongside English.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about official languages under the Constitution?
o: Under Article 345 a State may adopt one or more languages in use, or Hindi.
The Eighth Schedule now lists 22 languages.
The Eighth Schedule forms part of Part XVII.
Article 351 provides for the development of Hindi.
x: The Eighth Schedule (14 languages originally, now 22) is not part of Part XVII.

s: A Lieutenant Governor functions as the Administrator of a Union Territory under which Article?
x: Under Article 239, UTs are run by the President through an Administrator; the Governor's term is five years under Articles 153-162.

s: The Meghalaya Official Languages Ordinance, 2026 was promulgated under which Article?
x: A Governor promulgates ordinances under Article 213; the ordinance made Khasi and Garo official with English.

s: Within how many days did the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee propose that Governors decide on State List Bills?
x: It proposed a decision within 15 days on State List Bills, and reasons within 60 days for reserved Bills.

s: Which of the following pairs of Constitutional Amendment and language added to the Eighth Schedule is correctly matched?
x: The 92nd (2003) added Bodo, Santhali, Maithili and Dogri; the 21st added Sindhi, the 71st Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali, and the 102nd concerned the NCBC.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 239AA, giving Delhi the status of National Capital Territory?
x: The 69th Amendment (1991) inserted Article 239AA for the NCT of Delhi; the 14th Amendment inserted Article 239A for Puducherry.

s: Who was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh in the March 2026 changes?
x: Vinai Kumar Saxena moved from Delhi LG to LG of Ladakh; Kavinder Gupta moved from Ladakh to Himachal Pradesh.

s: In the March 2026 Governor changes, who was moved from Himachal Pradesh to become Governor of Telangana?
x: Shiv Pratap Shukla moved from Himachal Pradesh to Telangana, while Jishnu Dev Varma moved from Telangana to Maharashtra.

s: Which Article allows a State Legislature to adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as its official language?
x: Article 345 lets a State adopt one or more languages in use in the State, or Hindi, as official language.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule?
x: The 71st Amendment (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 21st added Sindhi and the 92nd added Bodo, Santhali, Maithili and Dogri.

s: How many languages are now listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
x: The Eighth Schedule began with 14 languages and now has 22.

s: Which Article provides for the Official Language Commission?
x: Article 344 provides for the Official Language Commission and Committee.

s: Whom did the Supreme Court ask to plan disability-friendly prisons on April 21, 2026?
o: The Rajya Sabha panel of Vice-Chairpersons
The bench headed by Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta
The committee headed by Justice Yashwant Varma
The committee headed by former judge Justice S. Ravindra Bhat
x: The Supreme Court asked the committee headed by former judge Justice S. Ravindra Bhat to plan disability-friendly prisons. The matter was heard by Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta, but they did not head the committee identified for this task.

s: Maneka Gandhi (1978) linked which Articles as the 'Golden Triangle'?
x: Maneka Gandhi linked Articles 14, 19 and 21 as the Golden Triangle and held the Passport Act reviewable.

s: What change did the Supreme Court make in Hamsanandini Nanduri v. Union of India regarding maternity leave for adoptive mothers?
o: Adoptive mothers are entitled to leave only after verification by the Authority
Only mothers adopting a child below 3 months are entitled to 12 weeks of leave
Adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks only when the child is below 3 years
All adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of leave irrespective of the child’s age
x: The Supreme Court struck down Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 and held that all adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of leave irrespective of the child’s age. The earlier rule limited the benefit to mothers adopting a child below 3 months.

s: Under Article 145(3), a substantial question of constitutional interpretation must be heard by at least how many judges?
x: Article 145(3) requires a bench of at least five judges, a Constitution Bench.

s: By what majority was the 2018 Constitution Bench verdict in the Sabarimala case delivered?
x: The 2018 verdict was 4:1, holding the exclusion unconstitutional; the matter was referred to a larger Bench in 2019.

s: In its suo motu proceedings following the November 2025 accidents in Rajasthan and Telangana, what did the Supreme Court recognise as part of the Right to Life under Article 21?
o: The right to safe travel on highways
x: The Supreme Court recognised safe travel on highways as part of the Right to Life under Article 21. Speedy trial, privacy and livelihood are associated with Hussainara Khatoon, K.S. Puttaswamy and Olga Tellis respectively.

s: In the Sabarimala review hearings, what did the Centre say rigid definitions of 'religious denomination' and 'essential religious practices' do?
o: Distort the plural nature of Hinduism
x: The Centre argued that rigid definitions distort the plural nature of Hinduism.

s: Article 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency because of which Constitutional Amendment?
x: After the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended in an Emergency; Article 21 also applies to non-citizens.

s: Under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, to which religions is Scheduled Caste status limited?
x: Clause 3 limits SC status to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists; conversion to other religions results in loss of the status.

s: In the Harish Rana case, what did the Supreme Court allow?
o: A right to die without any conditions
x: The Supreme Court allowed withdrawal of life support for Harish Rana, recognising the right to die with dignity as part of Article 21. This was the first time the Court actually implemented passive euthanasia in a specific case; active euthanasia remains illegal.

s: Which Constitution Bench is hearing the question of what constitutes an “industry” under labour law?
o: A nine-judge Constitution Bench led by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
A seven-judge bench led by Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
A five-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant
A nine-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant
x: A nine-judge Constitution Bench led by CJI Surya Kant is hearing what constitutes an industry under labour law. The hearings began on March 17, and the bench is re-examining the earlier legal position.

s:
Assertion (A): The Supreme Court actually implemented passive euthanasia in a specific case in the Harish Rana matter.
Reason (R): Active euthanasia remains legal in India.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true because the Harish Rana matter marked the first actual implementation of passive euthanasia in a specific case. Reason R is false because active euthanasia remains illegal; passive euthanasia involves withholding or withdrawing life-sustaining treatment under strict conditions.

s: Which of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh’s 1977 Government Order is incorrect?
o: It grants Scheduled Caste status after conversion to another religion.
It does not confer Scheduled Caste status.
It is distinct from the constitutional basis of Scheduled Caste status.
x: The incorrect statement is that the 1977 Government Order grants Scheduled Caste status after conversion to another religion. The Order provides only non-statutory concessions and does not confer SC status.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
o: Sikhs were added to it in 1956.
Buddhists were added to it in 1956.
A reconverted claimant must prove return, renunciation and acceptance by the original caste.
x: Buddhists were added in 1990, not 1956; Sikhs were added in 1956.

s: How did the Supreme Court treat Clinically Assisted Nutrition and Hydration (CANH) in the Harish Rana case?
o: Medical treatment that may be withdrawn in the patient's best interest
Basic care that can never be withdrawn
x: CANH was held to be medical treatment that may be withdrawn in the patient's best interest, with the family and medical boards involved.

s: Which Supreme Court case held that passive euthanasia could be permitted in exceptional cases?
o: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
Common Cause v. Union of India
Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
x: Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India (2011) held that passive euthanasia could be allowed in exceptional cases. Gian Kaur rejected a right to die, while Common Cause dealt with refusal of treatment and living wills.

s: The nine-judge Constitution Bench hearing the meaning of “industry” is re-examining which 1978 judgment?
o: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa
State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh
Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab
Common Cause v. Union of India
x: The case under re-examination is Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa (1978). State of UP v. Jai Bir Singh is a later reference concerning the development of the issue.

s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 19 May 2026, under what condition may rabid and incurably ill stray dogs be euthanised?
o: Only after examination by a veterinarian, in line with the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023
Immediately after being found near a school, hospital or bus station
Only after sterilisation under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960
Only on the recommendation of an Anti-Rabies Centre in every district
x: The Supreme Court permitted euthanasia of rabid and incurably ill stray dogs only after veterinary examination and in accordance with the Animal Birth Control Rules, 2023. The ruling did not permit immediate removal or euthanasia merely because dogs were found near public places; sterilised dogs were not to be released at the same public places.

s: Which 1954 case established the essential religious practices doctrine?
x: The Shirur Mutt case of 1954 established the essential religious practices doctrine.

s: Regarding the Sabarimala temple, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Location – Silent Valley National Park, Kerala
Age group of women barred – 12–45 years
x: The Travancore Devaswom Board administers Sabarimala; it is in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, penance lasts 41 days and women aged 10–50 were barred.

s: Under which Article was the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 issued?
x: The Order was issued under Article 341(1); only Parliament can amend the list under Article 341(2).

s: In determining an "industry", which test holds that the primary function decides the status?
x: Under the Dominant Nature Test the primary function decides the status; the Triple Test includes systematic activity.

s: What is the basis for Scheduled Caste classification?
x: Scheduled Caste classification is based on untouchability; Scheduled Tribe classification on tribal characteristics and isolation.

s: What is the status of the Industrial Disputes (Amendment) Act, 1982, which sought to exclude hospitals, education and sovereign functions?
o: Was struck down by the Supreme Court
Was referred to a Constitution Bench
x: The 1982 amendment was never notified.

s: Which Article of the Constitution, a Directive Principle, concerns the Uniform Civil Code?
x: Article 44 concerns the Uniform Civil Code under the Directive Principles of State Policy.

s: Which case recognised the right to refuse treatment and dealt with living wills, whose guidelines were simplified in 2023?
o: Aruna Shanbaug v. Union of India
Common Cause v. Union of India
x: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018) recognised the right to refuse treatment and addressed living wills; the guidelines were simplified in 2023. Aruna Shanbaug concerned passive euthanasia in exceptional cases.

s: Which one of the following case–right pairs is incorrectly matched?
o: Hussainara Khatoon — Right to speedy trial
x: The incorrectly matched pair is Common Cause — Right to livelihood. Common Cause is associated with the right to die with dignity, including passive euthanasia, whereas the right to livelihood was recognised in Olga Tellis.

s: Which case overruled P. Rathinam (1994), which had recognised a right to die under Article 21?
o: Gian Kaur v. State of Punjab (1996)
x: Gian Kaur (1996) rejected the right to die and overruled P. Rathinam.

s: Who delivered the lone dissent in the 2018 Sabarimala verdict?
x: The 2018 verdict was 4:1, with Justice Indu Malhotra dissenting; Rule 3(b) was struck down.

s: Under Hamsanandini Nanduri v. Union of India (2026), adoptive mothers get how many weeks of maternity leave regardless of the child's age?
x: The SC struck down Section 60(4) of the Code on Social Security, 2020, so all adoptive mothers get 12 weeks.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the 'Triple Test' for an 'industry' from Bangalore Water Supply (1978)?
o: Production or distribution of goods or services
x: Under the Triple Test, profit motive and capital are irrelevant.

s: In which case is the nine-judge Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant hearing the Sabarimala review?
o: Kantaru Rajeevaru v Indian Young Lawyers Association
S. Mahendran v Travancore Devaswom Board
Bijoe Emmanuel v State of Kerala
x: The Sabarimala review is Kantaru Rajeevaru v Indian Young Lawyers Association; hearing began on 7 April 2026 and judgment was reserved.

s: In which tiger reserve is the Sabarimala temple located?
x: The Sabarimala temple lies in the Periyar Tiger Reserve, Kerala.

s: Which case recognised the right to a speedy trial as part of Article 21?
x: Hussainara Khatoon (1979) linked speedy trial to Article 21; Olga Tellis (1985) dealt with livelihood.

s: Since 2017, how many weeks of maternity leave does the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 provide?
x: Maternity leave was raised to 26 weeks in 2017.

s: In which Andhra Pradesh case was it held that the right to life does not include the right to die?
o: AVS Narasimha Rao v. State of A.P.
Sunanda Reddy v. State of A.P.
P. Rathinam v. Union of India
Chenna Jagadeeswar v. State of A.P.
x: Chenna Jagadeeswar v. State of A.P. held that the right to life does not include the right to die.

s: The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze on Lok Sabha seats until the first Census after which year?
x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze until the first Census after 2026; the 42nd Amendment had frozen seats on the 1971 Census.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The 131st Amendment Bill received 298 votes in favour and 230 against.
The 106th Amendment Act is valid for 15 years.
The 84th Amendment froze Lok Sabha seats until 2000.
The Women's Reservation Bill was first introduced in 1996.
x: It was the 42nd Amendment that froze seats until 2000; the 84th Amendment extended the freeze.

s: At present, what Census basis is used for inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats and for constituency boundaries, respectively?
o: 1971 Census for inter-State allocation and 2001 Census for constituency boundaries
2001 Census for inter-State allocation and 1971 Census for constituency boundaries
1971 Census for both inter-State allocation and constituency boundaries
2001 Census for both inter-State allocation and constituency boundaries
x: Inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats is based on the 1971 Census, while constituency boundaries are based on the 2001 Census. The most tempting trap is reversing these two Census bases.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposal to expand the Lok Sabha to about 816 seats?
o: It aims to implement women's reservation without waiting for post-Census delimitation.
It is intended to apply from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
About 273 seats would go to women.
It would change each State's proportion of Lok Sabha seats.
x: The proposal keeps the States' proportions of seats unchanged; it avoids waiting for post-Census delimitation and is to operate from the 2029 polls.

s: With reference to the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, which pair is wrongly matched?
o: Proposed maximum strength of the Lok Sabha – 850 members
Earlier constitutional maximum of the Lok Sabha – 850 members
Articles amended for delimitation and women's reservation – Articles 81, 82 and 334A
Schedule mechanism – State-wise seats with each State's percentage share unchanged
x: The earlier maximum was 550 members; 850 is the proposed maximum.

s: What does the special majority needed for a constitutional amendment raising the number of Lok Sabha seats consist of?
o: A simple majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds of members present and voting plus a majority of the total membership
A majority of the total membership only
x: The special majority is two-thirds of members present and voting together with a majority of the total membership.

s: The Centre is considering delimitation to implement the Women's Reservation Act, 2023 before the 2029 polls on the basis of which Census?
x: The proposed delimitation is being considered on the basis of the 2011 Census.

s: Under the proposed Lok Sabha expansion for women's reservation, the House would grow from 543 to about how many seats?
x: Seats would rise from 543 to about 816, with about 273 for women, while the States' proportions stay unchanged.

s: In which year was the last delimitation exercise, based on the 2001 Census, completed?
x: The last exercise was completed in 2008 using the 2001 Census; the Commission was constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

s: What is the principle underlying the proposed redistribution of Lok Sabha seats?
o: One person, one vote, one value
x: The stated principle is "one person, one vote, one value"; Hindi-belt States such as Uttar Pradesh are expected to gain.

s: The 87th Amendment linked the delimitation of constituencies to which Census, while keeping seat totals frozen?
x: The 87th Amendment linked delimitation to the 2001 Census.

s: Under the government's 816-seat delimitation plan, the southern States' Lok Sabha seats rise from 129 to how many?
x: Southern seats go from 129 to 195, keeping their share at 23.8%.

s: Under the proposed temporary mechanism for additional women's seats in the Lok Sabha, how would approximately 273 seats be allotted to political parties?
o: According to the population of each State
According to their vote share in the last general election from pre-declared lists
x: Approximately 273 additional women's seats are proposed to be allotted to parties according to their vote share in the last general election from pre-declared lists. Equal distribution, State-population allocation and rotation after each delimitation are not the proposed temporary mechanism.

s: In which year was the Rajya Sabha established?
x: The Rajya Sabha was established in 1952; it has a maximum strength of 250 and a current strength of 245.

s:
Assertion (A): The proposal would increase the Lok Sabha strength from 543 to approximately 816 members.
Reason (R): The expansion would automatically trigger delimitation.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: The Assertion is true because the proposed strength is approximately 816 compared with the current 543. The Reason is false: the proposal specifically states that expansion does not automatically trigger delimitation. Therefore, the correct option is that A is true but R is false.

s: Regarding the Women's Reservation Act and delimitation, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Authority appointing the Delimitation Commission – President
Delimitation orders – Subject to judicial review
x: The President appoints the Delimitation Commission; the reservation lasts 15 years with sub-reservation for SC/ST women, and delimitation orders are not subject to judicial review.

s: How many votes did the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 get in favour in the Lok Sabha in April 2026?
x: It got 298 votes for and 230 against out of 528, short of the 326 needed, so it was defeated.

s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the Lok Sabha maximum from 550 to how many?
x: It sought a cap of 850 (815 from States and 35 from UTs) by amending Article 81.

s: How many times has the Delimitation Commission been constituted in India?
x: It was constituted four times: 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

s: Which Article bars courts from questioning delimitation orders?
x: Article 329(a) bars judicial review of delimitation orders, which have the force of law.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 131st Amendment package of 2026?
o: It proposed delimitation on the 2011 Census.
It included a Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
It automatically raised the strength of the Rajya Sabha.
x: Rajya Sabha strength under Article 80 does not change automatically; the other statements are correct.

s: Under Article 75(1A), the Council of Ministers may not exceed what share of the Lok Sabha strength?
x: Article 75(1A) caps the Council of Ministers at 15%, so an 850-member House would allow about 122 ministers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Delimitation Commission:
1. It is appointed by the President.
2. Its orders must be approved by Parliament.
3. It decides the SC/ST reserved constituencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Its orders have the force of law and are laid before Parliament only for information, so 2 is wrong; 1 and 3 are correct.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
x: The 104th Amendment (2019) ended Anglo-Indian nomination under Article 331 (Lok Sabha, 2 members) and Article 333 (Assemblies).

s: Besides a special majority in Parliament, what else did the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 need?
o: Ratification by half of the States
x: Because it touched representation of States, the 131st Amendment Bill needed a special majority and ratification by half of the State legislatures.

s: Under Article 80, what is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
x: Article 80 fixes the Rajya Sabha maximum at 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated); its current strength is 245.

s: Who elect the representatives of a State to the Rajya Sabha?
o: All members of the State Legislature, including MLCs
Elected members of the Legislative Assembly only
Members of the Lok Sabha from that State
x: Rajya Sabha members from a State are elected only by the elected MLAs (not MLCs), by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.

s: Under Article 170, what are the maximum and minimum strengths of a State Legislative Assembly?
x: Article 170 sets an Assembly at not more than 500 and not less than 60 members (Goa, Sikkim and Mizoram are exceptions).

s: Which Article provides for the abolition or creation of a State Legislative Council by an ordinary law of Parliament?
x: Under Article 169 Parliament may abolish or create a Council by ordinary law after the Assembly passes a special-majority resolution.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment first froze the inter-State allocation of Lok Sabha seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, until 2000?
x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze seats on the 1971 Census until 2000; the 84th extended the freeze.

s: In which years was the Delimitation Commission constituted in India?
x: Delimitation Commissions were set up four times: 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002.

s: From which date was the 106th Amendment Act (women's reservation) brought into force?
x: The Act, passed in September 2023, was brought into force from 16 April 2026 as a procedural step.

s: Which of the following statements about the ADR findings on Rajya Sabha members is incorrect?
o: One-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every 6 years.
36 Rajya Sabha members face serious criminal cases.
The Rajya Sabha has a maximum strength of 250, comprising 238 elected and 12 nominated members.
73 of 229 Rajya Sabha members face criminal cases.
x: The incorrect statement is that one-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every 6 years; they retire every 2 years. The six-year period is the term of an individual Rajya Sabha member, while the other three statements correctly report the ADR findings and constitutional composition.

s: The Union Cabinet’s decision on Vande Mataram was related to amending which legislation to protect the National Song on a footing equal to the National Anthem?
o: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
x: The Union Cabinet approved amending the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 to protect Vande Mataram like the National Anthem. The Citizenship Act, Official Languages Act and Representation of the People Act were not identified for this amendment.

s: Which Union ministry was associated with the invocation of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 during the Iran-linked energy crisis?
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
x: The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution was associated with the invocation of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. The other options are different Union ministries and were not identified for this action.

s: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 is implemented by which ministry?
x: The Act is implemented by the Ministry of Home Affairs; the Cabinet decided to amend it to protect Vande Mataram like the Anthem.

s: After Uttarakhand and Gujarat, which State in order did Assam become to pass a Uniform Civil Code Bill?
x: Assam became the third State, and the first in the Northeast, to pass a UCC Bill.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: They came into effect from 30 April 2026.
They provide for e-OCI with digital records and a centralised database.
They allow minors to hold both Indian and foreign passports.
x: Minors cannot hold both Indian and foreign passports under the rules; the other statements are correct.

s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 were notified by which ministry and came into force on 1 May 2026?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
x: The Rules were notified by MeitY and came into force on 1 May 2026 under Section 19 of the PROG Act, 2025. The Ministry of Home Affairs, Department of Financial Services and Ministry of Information and Broadcasting have representation in the Authority, but did not notify the Rules.

s: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, where is the Online Gaming Authority of India headquartered?
x: The Authority is headquartered in Delhi; the Rules contain 6 Parts and 26 Rules.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, is incorrect?
o: It provides a uniform law only on marriage and divorce, without covering inheritance or live-in relationships.
It requires registration of live-in relationships within one month.
It provides a uniform law on marriage, divorce, inheritance and live-in relationships.
x: The first statement is incorrect. The Bill covers marriage, divorce, inheritance and live-in relationships (live-in registration within one month), and it bans polygamy.

s: Which group is exempted from the provisions of the Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026?
x: Scheduled Tribes are exempted; pre-existing polygamous marriages are also protected.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the e-OCI provision under the Citizenship (Amendment) Rules, 2026?
o: It creates a database maintained separately by each State
It permits minors to hold both Indian and foreign passports
It abolishes OCI cards introduced in 2005
It provides digital records, physical or electronic OCI cards, and a centralised database
x: e-OCI provides digital records, physical or electronic OCI cards and a centralised database. The other options contradict the stated features by permitting dual passports for minors, abolishing OCI cards, or replacing the centralised database with separate State databases.

s: What does the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming (PROG) Act, 2025 ban?
x: The Act, passed in August 2025 and implemented in October 2025, bans online money games while promoting e-sports and online social games.

s: Under the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026, who acts as the appellate authority after a grievance reaches the Online Gaming Authority of India?
o: The Online Gaming Authority of India
x: The grievance route is from the service provider to the Authority within 30 days, followed by an appeal to the Secretary, MeitY. The Online Gaming Authority is the intermediate authority, not the appellate forum.

s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament, primarily seeks to achieve which of the following?
o: Abolition of all monetary and civil penalties for regulatory violations
Decriminalisation of minor offences and promotion of trust-based governance
Transfer of all regulatory disputes to criminal courts
Replacement of administrative adjudication with presidential review
x: The Bill decriminalises minor offences and promotes trust-based governance and ease of doing business. It does not abolish penalties; it converts certain criminal penalties into civil or monetary penalties.

s: Under the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, how often are fines revised upward by 10%?
x: Fines rise by 10% every three years, not five; imprisonment for minor offences is replaced by civil penalties.

s: Who chairs the six-member Online Gaming Authority of India?
o: Joint Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs
Joint Secretary, Department of Financial Services
x: The Authority is chaired by an Additional Secretary of MeitY; the Secretary, MeitY is the appellate authority.

s: Jan Vishwas 2.0 is linked to which World Bank framework?
x: Jan Vishwas 2.0 is linked to the World Bank's B-READY framework.

s: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 abolishes self-identification by removing which provision?
x: The Bill, introduced by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, removes Section 4(2).

s: Under the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, what rank must State representatives on the National Council hold?
x: The Bill requires State representatives on the National Council to be Director-level officers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, invoked in 2026?
o: It was invoked amid the Iran-linked energy crisis.
Section 3 of the Act regulates supply.
Violations may attract 3 months to 7 years' imprisonment with a fine.
It is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
x: The Act is administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; the other statements are correct.

s: Census 2011 recorded approximately how many transgender persons in India?
x: Census 2011 recorded about 4.88 lakh transgender persons, highest in Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra.

s: With reference to transgender rights in India, which pair is wrongly matched?
o: Transgender Persons Act, 2019 – Self-identification, DM certification and National Council
Virendra Kumar – Union Minister associated with the 2026 Amendment Bill
NALSA v. Union of India (2014) – Self-identification, DM certification and National Council
Post-recognition change – Gender can be changed in documents, including birth certificates
x: NALSA (2014) recognised the third gender and self-determination of gender identity; the DM certification and National Council framework came with the 2019 Act.

s: Which one of the following amendments removes self-determination of gender?
x: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in March 2026, removes Section 4(2) of the 2019 Act and so ends self-identification of gender.

s: In 2026, West Bengal made Vande Mataram compulsory in which assemblies of all recognised madrasas?
x: It was made compulsory in morning assemblies of madrasas, after being made mandatory in all schools.

s: Who composed Vande Mataram, which marked 150 years?
x: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay; Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana.

s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 amends 784 provisions in how many Central Acts?
x: It amends 784 provisions in 79 Central Acts run by 23 ministries; 717 are decriminalised.

s: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
x: It was introduced by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Minister Virendra Kumar).

s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Rules, 2026 contain how many Rules?
x: The Rules have 6 Parts and 26 Rules and were notified under Section 19 of the 2025 Act.

s: Under the Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, within how long must a live-in relationship be registered?
x: The Bill requires live-in relationships to be registered within one month; it also bans polygamy.

s: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, is associated with which of the following provisions?
o: Regulation of only educational online games
A ban on real-money games and establishment of an Online Gaming Authority of India under the 2026 Rules
Transfer of online gaming regulation exclusively to State Governments
A ban on all forms of online games, including recreational games
x: The Act bans real-money games, while the 2026 Rules establish the Online Gaming Authority of India from 1 May 2026.

s: Why is the Assam Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026 significant?
o: A Union law applicable only to Parliament
The second UCC Bill in the North-East and the fifth at the State level
The first UCC Bill in India and the first in the North-East
The first UCC Bill in the North-East and the third at the State level in India
x: The Assam UCC Bill, 2026 was described as the first such Bill in the North-East and the third State-level UCC Bill overall.

s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 amended how many provisions in 42 Central laws?
x: The 2023 Jan Vishwas Act amended 183 provisions in 42 Central laws; Jan Vishwas 2.0 amends 784 provisions in 79 Acts.

s: What is the position of the Speaker during debate on a resolution for the Speaker's removal?
o: Can speak and vote in the first instance but has no casting vote
Presides and has a casting vote
Can vote only in case of a tie
x: The Speaker can speak and vote in the first instance during the removal debate but cannot exercise a casting vote.

s: During the Budget Session, the Opposition moved a motion for the removal of which Lok Sabha Speaker?
x: The Opposition moved the motion against Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. G.V. Mavalankar, Hukam Singh and Balram Jakhar were Speakers against whom earlier removal motions had been moved, and all those motions failed.

s: Against whom did Congress MP K.C. Venugopal give a privilege notice over remarks on opposition MPs?
x: The privilege notice was against PM Narendra Modi; in the Lok Sabha such notices fall under Rule 187 (Rule 222 in the Rajya Sabha).

s: Who certifies a Bill as a Money Bill?
x: The Lok Sabha Speaker certifies Money Bills; the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional provisions on the Lok Sabha Speaker?
o: Article 96 provides that the Speaker shall preside while a removal resolution is under consideration.
Article 94(c) provides for removal by a resolution passed by a majority of all the members.
Article 93 provides for the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
Article 100 provides for a casting vote in the event of a tie.
x: Article 96 prevents the Speaker from presiding while a resolution for his removal is under consideration.

s: What procedural requirement applies before a motion for removal of the Lok Sabha Speaker can be taken up?
o: Seven days’ oral notice supported by 25 members
14 days’ written notice to the Speaker supported by at least 25 members
30 days’ written notice to the President supported by at least 100 members
14 days’ written notice to the Secretary-General supported by at least 50 members
x: The requirement is 14 days’ written notice to the Secretary-General, supported by at least 50 members. The other options alter the notice period, recipient or minimum support.

s: In the reported merger of seven of the ten AAP Rajya Sabha MPs with the BJP, the claimed protection under the Tenth Schedule was based on which requirement?
o: A merger supported by two-thirds of the members of the legislature party
A merger supported by one-third of the members of the legislature party
Approval by the President of India
Certification by the Election Commission of India
x: The MPs claimed protection because the Tenth Schedule permits a merger supported by two-thirds of the legislature party. The earlier one-third split provision was removed by the 91st Amendment, 2003.

s: Harivansh’s re-election as Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was notable for which distinction?
o: He became the first Deputy Chairman elected under the Tenth Schedule
He became the first member elected by secret ballot to become Deputy Chairman
He became the first nominated member to become Deputy Chairman
He became the first Deputy Chairman elected by the President
x: Harivansh became the first nominated member to become Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. He was nominated by President Droupadi Murmu and was elected through a voice vote under the applicable Rajya Sabha procedure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the anti-defection law?
o: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.
Disqualification is decided by the President or the Election Commission.
Kihoto Hollohan held the Speaker's decision subject to judicial review.
x: Disqualification is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, not the President or ECI.

s: Who became the first BJP Chief Minister of Bihar?
x: Samrat Choudhary was sworn in at Patna as Bihar's first BJP Chief Minister after Nitish Kumar's resignation.

s: Under the anti-defection law, when is a nominated member disqualified for joining a political party?
o: within 15 days of taking the seat
within 6 months of taking the seat
after 6 months of taking the seat
after 1 year of taking the seat
x: A nominated member attracts disqualification on joining a party after 6 months, not within 6 months.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about anti-defection case law?
o: Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) asked for decisions within 6 months.
Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) suggested an independent tribunal.
Padi Kaushik Reddy (2025) sought timely decisions without fixing a deadline.
Kihoto Hollohan (1992) made the Speaker's decision subject to judicial review.
x: Keisham Meghachandra Singh set a 3-month limit, not 6 months.

s: In the November 2025 Bihar Assembly election, how many of the 243 seats did the NDA win?
x: The NDA won 202 of 243 seats, with the BJP winning 89 and JD(U) 85.

s: What is MLATrack.com, launched by the Kerala Assembly?
o: A public grievance portal of the Assembly
A platform tracking MLAs' legislative work
A digital library of Assembly debates since 1957
x: MLATrack.com is India's first platform to track MLAs' legislative work, covering Kerala's 2021–2026 Assembly and over 68,000 questions and debates.

s: The 91st Amendment, 2003 removed which exception from the anti-defection law?
o: Defiance of whip condoned in 15 days
x: The 91st Amendment removed the one-third 'split' exception but kept the two-thirds merger protection.

s: According to ADR, which national party received no donations above Rs 20,000 for 19 years?
x: BSP declared no donation above Rs 20,000 for 19 years; BJP received Rs 6,074 crore in 2024-25.

s: Under which Article can the Lok Sabha Speaker be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House?
x: Article 94(c) provides for removal of the Speaker by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House.

s: Which case held that the Speaker's decision under the Tenth Schedule is subject to judicial review?
x: Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) upheld the Tenth Schedule but held the Speaker's decision open to judicial review.

s: In which case (2025) involving Telangana did the Supreme Court call for timely decisions on defection petitions, without fixing a deadline?
o: Padi Kaushik Reddy v. State of Telangana
x: Padi Kaushik Reddy v. Telangana (2025) asked for timely decisions on defection pleas but fixed no deadline.

s: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
x: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Articles 64, 89) and has only a casting vote.

s: After the November 2025 Bihar Assembly election, Nitish Kumar was sworn in as Chief Minister for which time?
x: After the November 2025 Bihar election Nitish Kumar was sworn in for a record 10th time; he later moved to the Rajya Sabha.

s: In the November 2025 Bihar Assembly election, which party emerged as the largest party?
x: The NDA won 202 of 243 seats; the BJP (89) was the largest party, JD(U) 85.

s: Under Article 124(1) of the Constitution, the Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and what else?
o: Such number of other judges as the Election Commission may prescribe
Such number of other judges as Parliament may prescribe by law
Such number of other judges as the President may prescribe without legislation
Such number of other judges as the Supreme Court Collegium may prescribe
x: Article 124(1) provides for the Chief Justice of India and such number of other judges as Parliament may prescribe by law. The constitutional provision does not assign this prescription to the Election Commission, the President acting without legislation, or the Collegium.

s: Till which date was the tenure of tribunal members extended?
x: The tenure of tribunal members was extended till 8 September 2026.

s: Which of the following cases was associated with striking down parts of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
o: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
Benazeer Heena v. Union of India
S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India
ADR v. Election Commission of India
x: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India was associated with the striking down of parts of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.

s: Justice Arun Palli, recommended for elevation to the Supreme Court in 2026, came from which High Court?
x: Arun Palli came from the J&K and Ladakh HC; Sheel Nagu came from Punjab & Haryana, S. Chandrashekhar from Bombay and Sanjeev Sachdeva from Madhya Pradesh.

s: To whom did Justice Yashwant Varma address his resignation before impeachment proceedings advanced?
x: Justice Yashwant Varma resigned to the President; resignation lets him keep pension and benefits.

s: Who was appointed Chief Justice of the Madras High Court in March 2026?
x: Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari became Chief Justice of the Madras High Court, succeeding Justice Manindra Mohan Shrivastava.

s: The judicial digitisation initiative ‘One Case One Data’ is designed to create which of the following?
o: A database linking only the 25 High Courts to the National Legal Services Authority
A paperless judiciary limited to Sikkim’s 32 judicial seats
A unified database linking 20,000+ taluka and district courts and 25 High Courts to the Supreme Court’s Case Information System
A network connecting 20,000+ taluka and district courts exclusively to the Supreme Court Registry’s chatbot
x: One Case One Data provides a unified database linking more than 20,000 taluka and district courts and 25 High Courts with the Supreme Court’s Case Information System. It is not limited to Sikkim, the High Courts alone, or the Su Sahay chatbot.

s: What is the proposed total strength of the Supreme Court in 2026, including the Chief Justice of India?
x: The strength was 8 in 1950 and 31 in 2008, and is proposed at 38 in 2026.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about court modernisation and Lok Adalat initiatives?
o: The court modernisation committee is to submit its report by 31 May 2026.
The court modernisation committee is headed by Justice Aravind Kumar.
The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is linked with 2007.
Samadhan Samaroh–2026 is a special Lok Adalat scheduled for 21–23 August 2026.
x: The committee is to report by 31 August 2026; 31 May 2026 was the last date for Samadhan Samaroh registration.

s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, where is the National Tribunals Commission headquartered?
x: The Commission's headquarters is New Delhi; it has five members with a five-year tenure or up to age 70.

s: On which date was Sikkim declared India's first fully paperless judiciary State?
x: CJI Surya Kant declared Sikkim fully paperless on 1 May 2026 at Gangtok; Su Sahay was launched on 11 May by NIC and the SC Registry.

s: What is the AI legal assistant launched under the DISHA programme, with Dishika as its mascot, called?
x: Nyaya Setu is the AI legal assistant under DISHA, built on Digital India Bhashini; Dishika is its mascot.

s: When is the Supreme Court's special Lok Adalat 'Samadhan Samaroh 2026' scheduled?
x: The special Lok Adalat runs from 21 to 23 August 2026, with registration closing on 31 May 2026.

s: Who heads the court modernisation committee whose report is due on 31 August 2026?
x: Justice Aravind Kumar heads the committee, with a target of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore.

s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, tribunal members hold office for 5 years or until what age?
x: The Bill, which replaces the 2021 Act, sets a tenure of 5 years or age 70.

s: The Supreme Court's sanctioned strength, including the CJI, was set at 31 by the Act of which year?
x: The 2008 Act set 31; the 2019 Act raised it to 34 and the 2026 Bill proposes 38.

s: Which of the following pairs (Act – Supreme Court strength including the CJI) is correctly matched?
x: The 1960 Act set 14; the 1977 Act set 18, 1986 set 26, 2008 set 31 and 2019 set 34, with 38 proposed in 2026.

s: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
x: Fathima Beevi became the first woman SC judge in 1989; Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court (HP, 1991).

s: Which bodies launched the Su-Sahayak AI chatbot on 11 May 2026?
o: NIC and the Supreme Court Registry
x: Su-Sahayak (Su Sahay) was launched by NIC and the Supreme Court Registry, not by NALSA.

s: Who was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in India?
x: Leila Seth became Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 1991, the first woman HC Chief Justice.

s: Who was the Attorney General of India in 2026?
x: R. Venkataramani is the Attorney General (Article 76); Tushar Mehta is the Solicitor General.

s: Under which Act was NALSA set up in 1995?
x: NALSA was set up in 1995 under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (in force 1995).

s: Which State became India's first fully paperless judiciary State on 1 May 2026?
x: CJI Surya Kant declared Sikkim India's first fully paperless judiciary State at Gangtok on 1 May 2026.

s:
Regarding the panel for appointing Election Commissioners, consider the following statements:
1. Under the interim arrangement in Anoop Baranwal, the Chief Justice of India was a member.
2. Under the 2023 Act, the Chief Justice of India continues to be a member.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The interim panel included the CJI; the 2023 Act replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM.

s: What phrase did the Supreme Court use on 7 May 2026 to describe Parliament’s long delay in making a law for the appointment of Election Commissioners?
x: The Supreme Court described Parliament’s long delay as the “tyranny of the elected.” The phrase was used by Justice Dipankar Datta; the other options alter the key expression.

s: Under Article 324(2), who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners?
x: Article 324(2) assigns the appointment to the President, subject to a law made by Parliament.

s: Under Article 324(5), on whose recommendation alone can an Election Commissioner be removed?
x: An Election Commissioner can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation, while the CEC is removable like a Supreme Court judge.

s: In the Bihar SIR petitions, the Supreme Court upheld which body's power to conduct the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls?
x: The Supreme Court held that the Election Commission can conduct the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Election Commission of India?
o: It is a constitutional body under Article 324.
The CEC's tenure is 6 years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.
The selection committee includes the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
The selection committee includes the Chief Justice of India.
x: The committee includes a Union Cabinet Minister in place of the Chief Justice of India.

s: On which date was the Election Commission of India set up?
x: The ECI was set up on 25 January 1950, a day before the Constitution came into force.

s: Why did the Rajya Sabha Chairman and Lok Sabha Speaker reject the notices seeking removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar?
o: No prima facie case of proved misbehaviour
Too few MPs had signed the notices
The notices were not addressed to the President
The CEC's term was about to end
x: The notices (signed by 63 Rajya Sabha and 130 Lok Sabha MPs) were rejected for want of a prima facie case of proved misbehaviour.

s: What principle did the Supreme Court lay down in Mohinder Singh Gill (1978) regarding Article 324?
o: Article 324 gives the Election Commission plenary powers where the law is silent
Article 324 makes the CEC subordinate to the other Election Commissioners
Article 324 requires the selection committee to include the Chief Justice of India
Article 324 prohibits the Election Commission from conducting legislative elections
x: Mohinder Singh Gill held that Article 324 gives the Election Commission plenary powers where the law is silent. The other options contradict the stated holding or concern a different case.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in T.N. Seshan v. Union of India (1995)?
o: The CEC can be removed only after Union Cabinet approval
A multi-member Election Commission is valid and the CEC is not superior to other ECs in decisions
The Election Commission must be a single-member body
The CEC's view prevails over the other ECs in all decisions
x: The Court upheld the multi-member Election Commission and held that the CEC is not superior to the other Election Commissioners in decision-making.

s: In the process for removing the Chief Election Commissioner, the inquiry committee has how many members?
x: A three-member inquiry committee examines the charges; the notice needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members.

s: Which of the following about the removal of Election Commissioners is NOT correct?
o: Other ECs are removed by the President on the recommendation of the CAG.
A similar process applies to Supreme Court judges under Article 124.
Other ECs are removed by the President on the recommendation of the CEC.
A similar process applies to the removal of the CAG.
x: Other Election Commissioners are removed on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner, not the CAG.

s: In ADR v. ECI, from which provisions did the Supreme Court hold the power to conduct the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls mainly flows?
o: Article 143 and the Citizenship Act, 1955 only
Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950
Article 356 and the Representation of the People Act, 1951
x: The Court held that the Election Commission's power to conduct Special Intensive Revision flows from Article 324 of the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the appointment of the CEC and Election Commissioners?
o: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister.
The Search Committee prepares a shortlist of five.
The Selection Committee can appoint only from the shortlist.
x: Section 8 allows the Selection Committee to go beyond the shortlist.

s: Under the 2023 Act on appointing Election Commissioners, who heads the Search Committee?
x: The Search Committee is headed by the Law Minister with two senior bureaucrats and prepares a shortlist of five.

s: On which date did Gyanesh Kumar become Chief Election Commissioner?
x: Gyanesh Kumar became CEC on 19 February 2025, succeeding Rajiv Kumar, who retired on 18 February 2025.

s: How many members must sign a notice of motion for the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner?
o: 50 Lok Sabha or 25 Rajya Sabha members
100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members
150 Lok Sabha or 75 Rajya Sabha members
200 Lok Sabha or 100 Rajya Sabha members
x: Like an SC judge, the CEC's removal motion needs a notice signed by 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members.

s: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner?
o: 5 years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
x: The CEC and ECs hold office for 6 years or till 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

s: Up to which year was the Election Commission of India a single-member body?
x: The ECI was a single-member body until 1989, when Election Commissioners were first added.

s: Which of the following about the cVIGIL app of the Election Commission is NOT correct?
o: It is used to report Model Code of Conduct violations
Photos and videos uploaded are geo-tagged
The ECI aims to act on complaints within 100 minutes
It is meant for candidates to seek permissions for rallies
x: Permissions for candidates are handled through Suvidha; cVIGIL is for citizens to report MCC violations.

s: What principle concerning arrest was laid down in Joginder Kumar v Uttar Pradesh?
o: Police Complaints Authorities must be established
The State must compensate for custodial death
Every arrest requires a medical examination of the arrested person
x: Joginder Kumar v Uttar Pradesh held that arrest must not be arbitrary. Compensation for custodial death, arrest-related safeguards and Police Complaints Authorities belong to other listed safeguards.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Forest Rights Act-related High Court rulings is incorrect?
o: The Allahabad High Court upheld the District Level Committee’s rejection of Tharu tribe claims.
The Madras High Court upheld eviction notices and grazing bans under the Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882 despite pending FRA claims.
The doctrine lex posterior derogat priori means that a later law overrides an earlier law.
Grazing rights are recognised even in national parks and sanctuaries.
x: The first statement is incorrect: the Allahabad High Court set aside, not upheld, the DLC's rejection of Tharu claims. The Madras HC did uphold eviction notices and grazing bans under the TN Forest Act, 1882; lex posterior derogat priori means a later law overrides an earlier one; and the FRA gives grazing rights even in national parks and sanctuaries.

s: How did the Madhya Pradesh High Court characterise the Bhojshala Complex in Dhar district?
o: As the Kamal Maula Mosque, established by the Archaeological Survey of India in 1861
As a historically Saraswati Temple and centre of Sanskrit learning linked to King Bhoja of the Parmar dynasty
As a complex used exclusively for Muslim prayers on Fridays under the 2003 arrangement
As a modern Sanskrit-learning centre managed solely by the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India
x: The Madhya Pradesh High Court held that the Bhojshala Complex was historically a Saraswati Temple and a centre of Sanskrit learning linked to King Bhoja of the Parmar dynasty. The name Kamal Maula Mosque is used by Muslims, while the Centre and ASI were to decide management; the complex was not characterised as exclusively a Friday-prayer site or as an ASI-established modern centre.

s: Which court awarded the death penalty to nine policemen in the Sattankulam custodial murder case?
o: Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court
x: A Tamil Nadu trial court sentenced nine policemen to death, calling it a rarest of rare case.

s: What can the National Human Rights Commission do in cases of custodial death?
x: The NHRC can recommend action but cannot punish officials.

s: What was held in Nilabati Behera v Odisha regarding custodial death?
o: Police stations must have mandatory CCTV
Procedure must be fair, just and reasonable
The State is liable to compensate for custodial death
x: Nilabati Behera v Odisha established State liability to compensate for custodial death. The principles concerning arbitrary arrest, fair procedure and CCTV are associated with other cases.

s: Regarding custodial safeguards, which case–outcome pair is correctly matched?
o: D.K. Basu v West Bengal – Mandatory CCTV in police stations
Prakash Singh v Union of India – Police Complaints Authorities
Paramvir Singh Saini v Baljit Singh – Arrest memo and medical examination
D.K. Basu v West Bengal – Police Complaints Authorities
x: Prakash Singh led to Police Complaints Authorities; D.K. Basu laid down arrest safeguards and Paramvir Singh Saini mandated CCTV.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, until when may forest dwellers NOT be evicted?
o: the State Forest Act is amended
verification of their claims is complete
the Gram Sabha holds a referendum
x: The FRA bars eviction until verification is complete; the Gram Sabha has the central role in recognising rights.

s: Under the Forest Rights Act, which body has the central role in recognising rights?
x: The Gram Sabha is central, and eviction cannot take place until verification is complete.

s: Which case led to CCTV cameras being required in police stations?
o: Prakash Singh v. Union of India
x: Paramvir Singh Saini concerns CCTV in police stations; D.K. Basu gave arrest safeguards and Prakash Singh Police Complaints Authorities.

s: Which doctrine did the Allahabad High Court apply in holding that the Forest Rights Act overrides earlier laws?
x: Lex posterior derogat priori means a later law overrides an earlier one; the HC set aside the DLC's rejection of Tharu claims.

s: Which international convention has India not ratified, a gap noted after the Sattankulam custodial murder verdict?
o: Convention on the Rights of the Child
Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
x: India has signed but not ratified UNCAT and has no anti-torture law.

s: Which case laid down arrest safeguards such as the arrest memo, informing a relative and medical examination?
o: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1997)
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
x: D.K. Basu v. West Bengal (1997) laid down arrest safeguards: memo, informing a relative and medical examination.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the NHRC in custodial death cases?
o: Custodial deaths must be reported to it within 24 hours
It can punish the guilty police officers
x: The NHRC can only recommend; it cannot punish.

s: Under the 73rd Amendment, which Article provides for the State Finance Commission, constituted every five years?
x: Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission; Article 243K for the State Election Commission.

s: To which of the following does the 33% reservation for women under the Women's Reservation Act, 2023 NOT apply?
o: Seats reserved for SCs and STs
x: The reservation does not apply to the Rajya Sabha; it includes seats reserved for SCs and STs.

s: The District Planning Committee under Article 243ZD was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 243ZD and the District Planning Committee belong to the 74th Amendment; the 73rd inserted Part IX on Panchayats.

s: Article 332A, inserted by the Women's Reservation Act, 2023, relates to which of the following?
x: Article 332A covers State Assemblies; 330A covers the Lok Sabha and 334A commencement and duration.

s: The intermediate tier of Panchayati Raj is optional for States with a population below what limit?
x: The intermediate tier is optional for States with a population below 20 lakh.

s: With which year is the Geeta Mukherjee committee on women's reservation associated?
x: The Geeta Mukherjee committee is associated with 1996; the Margaret Alva committee with 1987.

s: According to the Centre’s 2025 data, what percentage of elected Panchayati Raj Institution representatives were women?
x: Women constituted 49.7% of elected PRI representatives, amounting to 12.14 lakh out of 24.41 lakh. The tempting figure of 50% refers to the reservation provided by 19 States/UTs, while the constitutional minimum under Article 243D is one-third.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Women's Reservation Act, 2023:
1. It provides a sub-quota for OBC women.
2. It applies to the Delhi Legislative Assembly.
3. It is valid for 15 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The quota covers the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly for 15 years; there is no OBC sub-quota.

s: Which Article of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of the seats in Panchayats for women?
x: Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats and chairpersons' posts in Panchayats for women; the Constitution does not mandate 50%.

s: How many subjects are listed in the Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment?
x: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment (in force 24 April 1993), lists 29 subjects for Panchayats.

s: On which date did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment come into force?
x: The 73rd Amendment (1992) came into force on 24 April 1993, adding Part IX (Articles 243-243O).

s: Which Article of the Constitution fixes a five-year term for Panchayats?
x: Article 243E gives Panchayats a 5-year term; fresh polls must be held within 6 months of dissolution.

s: Which Article provides for the State Election Commission for Panchayat elections?
x: Article 243K provides for the State Election Commission; Article 243I for the State Finance Commission.

s: In which year did the Rajya Sabha pass the Women's Reservation Bill, which later lapsed?
x: The Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010 but lapsed; it was enacted in 2023.

s: Census 2027 will be conducted under the Census Act of which year?
x: Census 2027 runs under the Census Act, 1948 and Census Rules, 1990; the first Census was in 1872 and the first complete one in 1881.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Census 2027?
o: Sudarsan Pattnaik is the Registrar General of India.
The reference date for Population Enumeration is midnight of March 1, 2027.
The Census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.
x: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan is the Registrar General; Sudarsan Pattnaik is the brand ambassador.

s: Census 2027 will be India's first full caste enumeration since which year?
x: It is the first full caste enumeration since 1931, and India's first fully digital census.

s: For Census 2027, which organisation developed the digital tools including the House Listing Block Creator, HL Mobile App, Self-Enumeration Portal and CMMS?
x: C-DAC developed the digital tools for Census 2027, which is described as India’s first fully digital Census. The Registrar General of India is associated with administering the Census, but is not identified as the developer of these tools.

s: What was the Ministry of Home Affairs’ announcement regarding Naxalism in the country?
o: Its elimination only from Andhra Pradesh
Its complete elimination, with no affected districts remaining
Its classification as a movement beginning in 1967
x: The Ministry of Home Affairs announced the complete elimination of Naxalism and stated that there were no affected districts. The figure of 37 relates to the new Legacy and Thrust category, while 1967 marks the beginning of the Naxalbari movement.

s: What is the reference date for Census 2027?
x: The reference date is midnight of 1 March 2027; snowbound areas use 1 October 2026.

s: After declaring Naxalism eliminated, the MHA placed 37 districts in which new category?
x: 37 districts are in the new 'Legacy and Thrust' category; the other new category is 'Districts of Concern'.

s: What is the place of Census 2027 in the series of Indian Censuses?
x: Census 2027 is the 16th Census and the 8th since Independence; it is the first fully digital one.

s: In which year was the first complete (synchronous) Census held in India?
x: The first Census was in 1872 and the first complete Census in 1881.

s: What are the names of the mascots of Census 2027?
x: Census 2027's mascots are 'Pragati' and 'Vikas'; brand ambassador is Sudarsan Pattnaik.

s: Which Andhra Pradesh district figures in the new categories made by the MHA after it declared the elimination of Naxalism?
x: The notes list Alluri Sitharama Raju (AP) along with Bhadradri Kothagudem and Mulugu (Telangana) in the new categories.

s: The Telangana Assembly bill permanently removed which bar for Panchayat, Mandal and Zilla Praja Parishad polls?
x: The bill permanently removed the two-child bar for these local-body polls.

s: Following the State resolution, what name did the Union Cabinet approve for Kerala under Article 3?
x: The Union Cabinet approved renaming Kerala as 'Keralam' under Article 3.

s: As held in the Rajasthan High Court (1966) and Syed Habibullah cases, what is the effect of procedural defects in delivering the Governor's address?
o: Invalidate all proceedings of the session
Invalidate only the Bills passed in that session
Do not invalidate the legislative proceedings
Require the address to be delivered again
x: These cases held that procedural defects in delivery do not invalidate the proceedings.

s: Which Article deals with the oath of the Governor?
x: Article 159 deals with the Governor's oath; Article 163 concerns aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

s: Since which year has there been no Governor's address under Article 176 in Tamil Nadu?
x: In Tamil Nadu, portions of the address were skipped in 2022 and 2023, and there has been no Article 176 address since 2024.

s: Which recommendation is associated with the Punchhi Commission (2007)?
o: Limiting extra roles of the Governor, such as the role of Chancellor
Describing the Governor as the constitutional head acting on aid and advice
Holding that discretion cannot stall an elected government
Describing the Governor as the “lynchpin of cooperative federalism”
x: The Punchhi Commission (2007) recommended limiting extra roles of the Governor, including roles such as Chancellor. The other options correspond to Shamsher Singh, State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor of Tamil Nadu, and the Sarkaria Commission respectively.

s: Which body described the Governor as the 'lynchpin of cooperative federalism'?
x: The phrase is from the Sarkaria Commission (1988); Shamsher Singh held the Governor a constitutional head acting on aid and advice.

s: Under which Article does the Governor reserve Bills for the consideration of the President?
x: Bills are reserved under Article 200; Article 356 concerns President's Rule.

s: Along with approving the name 'Keralam', for whom did the Union Cabinet approve free HPV vaccination?
x: The Cabinet approved free HPV vaccination for girls of 14.

s: Who revoked the proclamation under Article 356(2) in Manipur on 4 February 2026?
x: President Droupadi Murmu revoked the proclamation under Article 356(2) on 4 February 2026. Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla and Yumnam Khemchand Singh were associated with the subsequent state government, not with revoking the proclamation.

s: Under the Kerala Nativity Card Bill, who is the issuing authority for the Nativity Card?
x: The Tahsildar issues the card; an appeal lies to the District Collector.

s: Who became the new Chief Minister of Manipur after the revocation of President’s Rule in February 2026?
x: Yumnam Khemchand Singh, the BJP legislature party leader, became the new Chief Minister of Manipur. Ajay Kumar Bhalla was the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

s: Under the Kerala Nativity Card Bill, on which event does the Nativity Card become invalid?
x: The card becomes invalid on acquiring foreign citizenship; it serves as official identity for state services, benefits and reservations.

s: When did Jharkhand notify its PESA Rules, after a gap of 25 years since the State’s formation?
x: Jharkhand notified its PESA Rules in January 2026, 25 years after the State was formed in 2000. The PESA Act was enacted in 1996, while 1992 refers to the 73rd Amendment.

s: C-Mitra, launched by Hyderabad City Police in January 2026, is India's first virtual helpdesk for whom?
x: C-Mitra is India's first virtual helpdesk for cybercrime victims, launched by Hyderabad City Police on 9 January 2026.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Bihar government's order on meat, fish and eggs?
o: It banned their sale near schools.
It banned their sale near temples.
It banned their consumption near schools and temples.
It banned their sale near educational institutions.
x: The order banned only the sale, not the consumption, of meat, fish and eggs near schools, educational institutions and temples.

s: In Telangana's police reorganisation, what was the Malkajgiri commissionerate renamed?
x:
App key: Rachakonda (stem says Malkajgiri was renamed Rachakonda). Strictly: Rachakonda was renamed Malkajgiri (Praveen CA-360 Jan 2026 p.60); Rachakonda is Malkajgiri's former name.
Rachakonda is the old name: the Telangana notification renamed the Rachakonda commissionerate as Malkajgiri, so the four are Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Malkajgiri and the new Future City. The stem has the renaming the wrong way round; Rachakonda is kept as the only option linked to Malkajgiri (its former name), while Future City is the new commissionerate and Cyberabad kept its name.

s: The PESA Act, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution to which areas?
x: PESA extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas; Jharkhand notified its PESA Rules in January 2026.

s: What is the minimum age for appointment as a Governor?
x: A Governor must be at least 35 years old and cannot be an MP or MLA.

s: In which case did a seven-judge bench hold in 1974 that the Governor is a constitutional head acting on the aid and advice of ministers?
x: Shamsher Singh (1974), a seven-judge bench, held that the Governor is a constitutional head bound by ministerial advice.

s: Under Article 176, when must the Governor address the State Legislature?
o: At the first session after a general election and at the first session of every year
Only at the first session after a general election
At the start of every session
Only when the Council of Ministers asks
x: Article 176 makes the Governor's address mandatory at the first session after each general election and the first session of every year.

s: On whose committee's recommendations was the PESA Act, 1996 based?
x: The Bhuria Committee (1994-95) recommended extending Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule areas, which led to the PESA Act, 1996.

s: Which domicile case from Andhra Pradesh, decided in 1995, is linked to the debate on the Kerala Nativity Card Bill?
o: Sunanda Reddy v. State of AP
AVS Narasimha Rao v. State of AP
Dr Pradeep Jain v. Union of India
Kailash Chand Sharma v. State of Rajasthan
x: Sunanda Reddy v. State of AP (1995) is a domicile case; AVS Narasimha Rao v. State of AP was in 1969.

s: From which provision of the Government of India Act, 1935 does the Governor's address under Article 176 originate?
x: The Governor's address has its origin in Section 63 of the GoI Act 1935, with the convention from April 1937.

s: Who was the Governor of Manipur when President's Rule was revoked in February 2026?
x: Ajay Kumar Bhalla was Manipur's Governor when Yumnam Khemchand Singh became CM in February 2026.

s: What is the toll-free number of the Telangana Anti-Corruption Bureau?
x: The Telangana ACB's toll-free number is 1064.

s: In Telangana's police reorganisation, which new commissionerate was created alongside Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Rachakonda?
x: Telangana now has 4 commissionerates around Hyderabad: Hyderabad, Cyberabad, Rachakonda (Malkajgiri renamed) and the new Future City.

s: Which pair of enactments was specifically associated with the Kerala Nativity Card Bill?
o: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 and Article 23
x: The Kerala Nativity Card Bill was related to the Citizenship Act, 1955 and the RBD Act, 1969, along with several constitutional provisions. The other pairs belong to legal-aid, bonded-labour or advocate-training contexts rather than the related framework specified for this Bill.

s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the rights of religious denominations?
x: Article 26 concerns religious denominations; Article 25 concerns individual freedom of religion.

s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits forced labour?
x: Article 23 prohibits forced labour, while Article 21 protects dignity.

s: Which Section of the BNS, 2023 includes organ removal within trafficking?
x: Section 143 of the BNS, 2023 includes organ removal within trafficking.

s: Which Supreme Court case concerned the ban on child labour in hazardous industries?
x: M.C. Mehta vs Tamil Nadu (1996) dealt with child labour in hazardous industries; Vishal Jeet treated trafficking as a socio-economic problem.

s: Women aged 10–50 were barred at Sabarimala because Lord Ayyappa is regarded as what?
x: The bar rested on Lord Ayyappa being a Naishtika Brahmachari; Justice Indu Malhotra's dissent emphasised respect for essential religious practice.

s: In the Sabarimala case, who proposed the Anti-Exclusion Test focusing on dignity and equality?
x: Justice D.Y. Chandrachud proposed the Anti-Exclusion Test; the September 2018 decision was 4:1.

s: Under which Article did the Supreme Court hold that solid waste management is part of the right to a healthy environment?
x: The Court held that a clean environment is intrinsic to Article 21 and treated solid waste management as part of the right to a healthy environment.

s: In Dr Jay Thakur v. Union of India, menstrual health was recognised as part of which Article?
x: In Dr Jay Thakur v Union of India, menstrual health was held part of Article 21 (dignity, privacy, bodily autonomy). It was also tied to Articles 14 and 21A.

s: The Supreme Court’s final arguments on review petitions concerning the Sabarimala entry dispute are being heard in which case?
o: Sastri Yagnapurushadji vs Muldas Bhudardas Vaishya
Dr Jay Thakur vs Union of India
Indian Young Lawyers Association vs State of Kerala (2018)
x: The review petitions are in Indian Young Lawyers Association vs State of Kerala (2018). Dr Jay Thakur vs Union of India concerned menstrual health as a fundamental right.

s: In Dr Jay Thakur vs Union of India, how was the provision of menstrual-health facilities characterised?
