o: A voluntary contribution, not a constitutional responsibility
A matter primarily outside Government of India concern
x: The provision of menstrual-health facilities was characterised as a constitutional responsibility, not charity. The other descriptions relate to different governance or religious-law issues.

s: In January 2026, the Supreme Court reserved its judgment in which case concerning a plea to withdraw life support?
o: Harish Rana vs Union of India
x: The Supreme Court reserved judgment in Harish Rana vs Union of India, 2025, concerning a plea to withdraw life support. Gian Kaur and Common Cause are other cases relating to the legal development of the right to die and living wills, while K.P. Kiran Kumar concerns child trafficking.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the right to die is correctly matched?
o: Gian Kaur – Right to die rejected
Common Cause – Right to die recognised by a High Court
x: Gian Kaur rejected the right to die. Maruti Dubal was the High Court recognition of the right to die, Aruna Shanbaug permitted passive euthanasia, and Common Cause recognised living wills.

s: The right to die with dignity, relevant in the Harish Rana case, is part of which Article?
x: Article 21 includes the right to die with dignity; passive euthanasia is legal under guidelines.

s: What does Article 17 of the Constitution deal with?
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; the Right against Exploitation is Articles 23-24.

s: In its 6 January 2026 ruling, what did the Delhi High Court hold regarding a woman's abortion under the MTP Act?
o: The woman's consent is sufficient; the husband's consent is not required
A woman commits an offence under IPC Section 312 if she undergoes an abortion
Abortion after 14 weeks is always prohibited
x: The Delhi High Court held that the MTP Act does not require the husband's consent for a woman's abortion. It also observed that forced continuation of pregnancy can amount to mental cruelty. The tempting contrary option is that the husband's consent is mandatory, but the ruling specifically rejected that requirement.

s: The Supreme Court's 2023 simplification of passive euthanasia reduced the experience requirement for board members from 20 years to how many years?
x: The reforms reduced the requirement to 5 years, with two boards, a three-member board and a 48-hour deadline.

s: Which case first saw a High Court recognise a right to die?
x: In Maruti Dubal (1987) a High Court recognised a right to die; Gian Kaur later rejected it.

s: In Dr Jay Thakur v. Union of India, for girls in which classes were free biodegradable sanitary pads directed?
x: The SC directed free biodegradable sanitary pads for girls in Classes 6 to 12, calling it a constitutional responsibility.

s: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which Section defines murder?
x: BNS: Section 100 culpable homicide, Section 101 murder, Section 108 abetment of suicide.

s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits the employment of children in factories, mines and hazardous work?
x: Article 24 prohibits child labour; Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour.

s: In which case (1990) did the Supreme Court treat trafficking as a socio-economic problem?
o: Vishal Jeet v. Union of India
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India
Gaurav Jain v. Union of India
x: Vishal Jeet (1990) treated trafficking as a socio-economic problem.

s: In Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India (2016), the Supreme Court directed the Centre to set up which fund under the Disaster Management Act, 2005?
x: The Court found the National Disaster Mitigation Fund under Section 47 of the DM Act, 2005 had never been set up and ordered it within three months.

s: Which Supreme Court bench delivered the drought-management judgment in Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India (May 2016)?
o: Justices Madan B. Lokur and N.V. Ramana
Justices T.S. Thakur and A.K. Sikri
Justices Dipak Misra and U.U. Lalit
Justices J.S. Khehar and R.F. Nariman
x: The 11 May 2016 judgment was given by Justices Madan B. Lokur and N.V. Ramana.

s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, which of the following activities is permitted for private entities in the nuclear sector?
o: Enrichment of U-235 beyond the prescribed limit
Operating nuclear plants and manufacturing equipment
Appearing before the Nuclear Damage Claims Commission
x: The SHANTI Act, 2025 permits private entities to operate plants, manufacture equipment, fabricate fuel and undertake enrichment of U-235 up to the prescribed limit. Enrichment beyond the limit and spent fuel management remain reserved for the Centre. Hence, operating nuclear plants and manufacturing equipment is correct.

s: The Kakrapar nuclear power plant is located in which State?
x: Kakrapar is in Gujarat; Tarapur is in Maharashtra, Rawatbhata in Rajasthan and Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu.

s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, which institution was granted statutory status and made accountable to Parliament?
x: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), established in 1983, was granted statutory status and made accountable to Parliament. The other options are bodies associated with nuclear-damage redressal or appeals, not the regulator receiving this status.

s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, what happened to supplier liability, and what covers liability above the cap?
x: The SHANTI Act eliminates supplier liability, and liability exceeding the applicable cap is covered by a Nuclear Liability Fund.

s: The SHANTI Bill, 2025 proposes to replace which existing laws?
o: Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and Electricity Act, 2003
Atomic Energy Act, 1948 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
Atomic Energy Act, 1948 and Electricity Act, 2003
x: The SHANTI Bill, 2025 proposes to replace the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.

s: The SHANTI Bill, 2025 ends the monopoly of which entity over nuclear power generation by allowing private and foreign participation?
x: The Bill proposes the first-ever private and foreign participation in nuclear power generation, ending the NPCIL monopoly.

s: Section 39 of the SHANTI Act, 2025 lets the Centre declare nuclear information 'restricted', overriding which law?
x: Section 39 lets the Centre declare nuclear information restricted and overrides the RTI Act.

s: In India's nuclear-energy framework, to which reactors do IAEA safeguards apply?
x: IAEA safeguards apply to reactors using imported uranium.

s: At what level does the SHANTI Act, 2025 cap nuclear liability?
x: The SHANTI Act caps liability at 300 million SDR and has no supplier liability.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's nuclear-sector framework?
o: Appeals under the nuclear-damage redressal mechanism lie with the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity
The Atomic Energy Act, 1948 replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962
India's new nuclear-power target is 100 GW by 2047
The SHANTI Act, 2025 replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010
x: The chronology is reversed: the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 replaced the 1948 Act.

s: The Atomic Energy Act, 1962, now replaced by the SHANTI Act, had itself replaced the Atomic Energy Act of which year?
x: The 1962 Act replaced the 1948 Act; SHANTI replaces both the 1962 Act and the CLND Act, 2010.

s: In which year was the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, given statutory status by the SHANTI Act, set up?
x: The AERB was set up in 1983 and is now statutory and accountable to Parliament.

s: What is India's target for nuclear power capacity by 2047?
x: Capacity is 8.18 GW now, with targets of 22 GW by 2032 and 100 GW by 2047.

s:
Consider the following statements about the SHANTI Act, 2025:
1. It retains supplier liability as under the CLND Act, 2010.

3. Spent fuel management remains with the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Supplier liability is eliminated, so 1 is wrong; the Liability Fund and the Centre's control of spent fuel are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SHANTI Bill, 2025?
o: Private and foreign firms may build, own, operate and decommission nuclear plants.
The government retains control over fuel production, heavy water and radioactive waste.
Operator liability is capped and linked to reactor capacity.

s: What outlay was announced for the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Union Budget 2025–26?
x: The Budget 2025–26 announced a Nuclear Energy Mission with ₹20,000 crore, towards the target of 100 GW by 2047.

s: In which State is the Kudankulam nuclear power plant located?
x: Kudankulam, a pressurised water reactor plant, is in Tamil Nadu.

s: What is the full form of the SHANTI Act, 2025, which opened the nuclear sector to private firms?
o: Safe Harnessing of Atomic and Nuclear Technology for India Act
Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act
Strategic Handling of Atomic and Nuclear Technology in India Act
Sustainable Harnessing of Atomic Nuclear Technology for India Act

x: Kakrapar - Gujarat, Tarapur - Maharashtra, Rawatbhata - Rajasthan, Kudankulam - Tamil Nadu.

s: What is India's nuclear power capacity target for 2032?
x: From 8.18 GW now, India targets 22 GW by 2032 and 100 GW by 2047.

s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, to which body do appeals go?
x: Appeals under the SHANTI Act go to the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity set up under the Electricity Act 2003.

s: In which year was the Official Secrets Act, which applies to defence personnel even after retirement, enacted?
x: The Official Secrets Act dates to 1923 and continues to apply after retirement.

s: The Naxalmukt Bharat Abhiyan set which deadline for eliminating Naxalism?
x: The target was 31 March 2026; 312 LWE cadres were eliminated in 2025, the highest ever.

s: According to the MHA Year End Review 2025, on which villages does the Vibrant Villages Programme focus?
x: The Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP and VVP-2) concerns border villages, not urban villages.

s: As per the MHA Year End Review 2025, what was the approximate conviction rate of the NIA?
x: The NIA conviction rate was approximately 95%, not 85%.

s: Along the border of which States was the biggest-ever anti-Naxal operation in the Karreguttalu Hills conducted?
x: The operation on the Chhattisgarh–Telangana border eliminated 31 Naxalites in 21 days with no SF casualties.

s: Who was the CPI-Maoist General Secretary eliminated at Narayanpur during the 2025 anti-Naxal operations?
x: Nambala Keshav Rao alias Basavaraju, the CPI-Maoist General Secretary, was eliminated at Narayanpur, the first such high-level elimination in three decades.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct according to the MHA Year End Review 2025?
o: I4C launched e-Zero FIR for automatic registration of FIRs in cyber financial crimes
The four-pillar cyber strategy comprises Convergence, Coordination, Communication and Capacity
The new criminal laws completed two years in 2025
x: The new criminal laws completed one year, not two, in 2025.

s: Which gap was identified in the legal framework surrounding the Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025?
o: There was no definition of digital “work”, and it was not explicitly linked to Article 21
There was no statutory definition of hate speech
There was no provision for caste-based insults
There was no provision for mob lynching guidelines
x: The identified gap was the absence of a definition of digital “work” and the lack of an explicit link to Article 21. The other options relate to hate-speech legislation or judicial guidelines, not the Right to Disconnect Bill.

s: Which pairing correctly describes how France and Germany approach digital communication and working hours?
o: France: collective bargaining on digital communication; Germany: strict hour caps
France: strict hour caps; Germany: strict hour caps
France: strict hour caps; Germany: collective bargaining on digital communication
France: collective bargaining; Germany: collective bargaining
x: France relies on collective bargaining on digital communication, while Germany relies on strict hour caps.

s: On which date was the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 first promulgated as an ordinance?
x: It was first promulgated as an ordinance on 25 October 1975 and completed 50 years in February 2026.

s: The Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025 was discussed against the backdrop of which Labour Code being silent on digital labour?
x: The Bill arose after 29 labour laws were consolidated into four Labour Codes, with the OSH Code, 2020 silent on digital labour.

s: What right does the Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025 give employees?
o: To respond to work calls beyond working hours for overtime pay
To work from home on two days a week
Not to respond to work calls and emails beyond working hours
x: The Bill's central provision is a right not to respond to work calls and emails beyond working hours.

s: What is the proposed Indian Scientific Service (ISS) intended to be?
o: A temporary scientific cadre replacing the IAS
A permanent scientific cadre replacing the IAS
A permanent All-India scientific cadre complementing the IAS
x: The ISS is proposed as a permanent All-India scientific cadre alongside the civil services, complementing rather than replacing the IAS.

s: Which of the following is an illustrative cadre proposed under the Indian Scientific Service?
x: Environmental & Ecological is one of the illustrative cadres proposed for the Indian Scientific Service.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the proposed Indian Scientific Service is incorrect?
o: It envisages national recruitment with peer evaluation.
It would embed scientists in ministries and regulators.
It would operate through separate service rules.
It would recruit scientists only through state-level examinations.
x: The incorrect statement is that recruitment would be only through state-level examinations. The proposal envisages national recruitment with peer evaluation, along with scientists embedded in ministries and regulators and separate service rules.

s: In which year was the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, which completed 50 years in February 2026, enacted?
x: It was enacted in 1976 after an ordinance of 25 October 1975; Article 23 bans forced labour.

s: Which I4C initiative registers an FIR automatically for cyber financial crimes?
x: I4C's e-Zero FIR registers FIRs automatically for cyber financial crimes.

s: In which year was PRAGATI, which held its 50th meeting, launched?
x: PRAGATI was launched in 2015 and has completed its 50th meeting.

s: As what type of Bill was the Right to Disconnect Bill, 2025 introduced?
x: It is a Private Member's Bill and India's first formal legislative attempt on after-hours digital work.

s: By what name was the operation in which the Pahalgam attackers were eliminated known?
x: The MHA Year End Review 2025 lists Operation Mahadev, in which the Pahalgam attackers were eliminated, besides Operation Sindoor.

s: How many labour laws were merged into the four Labour Codes?
x: 29 central labour laws were merged into four Labour Codes.

s: Where was the first India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management (IIC-DEM) held in January 2026?
x: IIC-DEM 2026 was held at Bharat Mandapam (21–23 January 2026), organised by IIIDEM.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about IICDEM–2026?
o: It brought together about 100 delegates from about 70 countries
It was held under CEC Rajiv Kumar
It was held at Bharat Mandapam
It featured 36 thematic groups and showcased the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls
x: The CEC at the time was Gyanesh Kumar, not Rajiv Kumar.

s: What minimum share of votes in the last election did a party need to be eligible to receive electoral bonds?
x: Eligibility required a party to have secured at least 1% of the votes in the last election.

s: How much did electoral trusts receive in donations in 2024–25?
x: Electoral trusts received ₹3,826.35 crore, of which the BJP got ₹3,157.66 crore.

s: In February 2024, for violating which Article did the Supreme Court strike down the Electoral Bonds Scheme?
x: The Court held that the scheme violated Article 19(1)(a), the right to information.

s: In which year did the CBDT introduce the Electoral Trusts Scheme?
x: CBDT introduced the Electoral Trusts Scheme in 2013.

s: Under the post-electoral-bond framework, what is not disclosed by an electoral trust?
o: Donor names to the Election Commission
Which company funded which political party
x: An electoral trust does not disclose which company funded which party. The other details, including donor names, amounts and recipient parties, are disclosed in its annual report to the Election Commission.

s: Which institution was the issuer of electoral bonds?
x: State Bank of India issued electoral bonds; Prudent Electoral Trust was an electoral trust, not the issuer.

s: ECINET, the single digital platform of the Election Commission, integrates more than how many ECI applications?
x: ECINET integrates 40+ ECI apps for about one billion voters and follows the RP Acts of 1950 and 1951.

s: Which platform has been described as a one-stop Election Commission of India platform for draft electoral rolls and related services?
x: The ECINET app is intended to function as a one-stop ECI platform providing access to draft electoral rolls and other services.

s: A citizen wishes to report a suspected violation of the election code, a candidate seeks permission for an election-related activity, and a voter with disability seeks accessible voter services. Which sequence of applications is appropriate?
x: cVIGIL is used by citizens to report code violations, Suvidha facilitates candidates' permissions, and Saksham serves persons with disabilities who vote.

s: Which statement correctly describes the legal ceiling on political expenditure?
o: Parties are capped but candidates are not capped
Both parties and candidates are subject to the same legal cap
There is no legal cap on party expenditure; only candidates are capped
There is no legal cap on either party or candidate expenditure
x: There is no legal cap on party expenditure, whereas candidates are subject to a cap. The other options incorrectly extend or remove the expenditure ceiling.

s: For whom is the ECI app 'Saksham' meant?
x: Saksham serves PwD voters; cVIGIL is for citizens and Suvidha for candidates.

s: Electoral bonds were valid for how many days from issue?
x: Electoral bonds, issued by SBI, were valid for 15 days.

s: During which period were corporate donations to political parties banned?
x: Corporate donations were banned from 1969 to 1985.

s: Through which institute did the ECI organise IICDEM-2026?
x: The ECI organised IICDEM-2026 through the India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM).

s: In Census 2027, self-enumeration through the apps is allowed up to how many days before field work?
x: Census 2027 allows self-enumeration through Android and iOS apps up to 15 days before field work.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Census 2027?
o: It is the 16th Census and the 8th after Independence.
It is conducted under the Census Act, 1948 and Census Rules, 1990.
Its budget is about Rs 11,718 crore.
Its caste count is the first since 1951.
x: Census 2027's caste enumeration is the first since 1931; the other statements are correct.

s: The electronically collected caste data in Census 2027 is India's first caste enumeration since which year?
x: Caste data in Census 2027 is collected electronically and marks the first caste enumeration since 1931.

s: After Census 2027 the freeze on inter-State Lok Sabha seat distribution ends. It will be the first redistribution since which year?
x: The redistribution after Census 2027 will be the first since the 1976 freeze; the 2002–08 exercise only redrew internal constituency boundaries.

s: In projections for an approximately 888-seat Lok Sabha, to about how many would Tamil Nadu's seats rise?
x: Tamil Nadu would go from 39 to about 53; UP is projected at 151, Bihar at 82 and Kerala at 23.

s: When is the House Listing and Housing Census (HLHC), the first phase of Census 2027, scheduled?
x: HLHC is scheduled for April–September 2026; February 2027 is the Population Enumeration phase.

s: Which statement regarding orders made by delimitation authorities is correct?
o: They lapse automatically after every general election.
They are routinely challengeable before every High Court.
They are not challengeable in court.
They can be challenged only by the Election Commission.
x: Orders relating to delimitation are not challengeable in court.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the freeze on Lok Sabha seats?
o: The 42nd Amendment froze seats on the 1971 Census.
The 84th Amendment extended the freeze till the first Census after 2021.
The freeze on inter-State seats ends after Census 2027.
The redistribution after Census 2027 would be the first since 1976.
x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze till the first Census after 2026, not 2021.

s: The 1976 freeze on inter-State Lok Sabha seat distribution (42nd Amendment) was based on the population of which Census?
x: The freeze introduced by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 was based on the 1971 population.

s: After which Census is the next readjustment of seats expected?
x: The next readjustment of seats is expected after Census 2027.

s: Which set of Articles is associated with delimitation and reservation of seats in the legislatures?
x: Articles 82, 170, 330 and 332 are the constitutional provisions identified in connection with delimitation and legislative reservations.

s: What did the 2002–08 Delimitation Commission do?
x: It only redrew internal boundaries on the 2001 Census; inter-State seats stayed frozen at 543.

s: Who moved the private member constitutional amendment Bill proposing judicial diversity and regional benches of the Supreme Court?
x: P. Wilson, a DMK Rajya Sabha MP, moved the private member constitutional amendment Bill. The other options are linked to the Manipur constitutional development or the Presidency, not to this Bill.

s: Which case created the collegium system for appointing judges?
x: The Second Judges case created the collegium system; the First Judges case resulted in executive primacy.

s: What nomination fee did the Supreme Court specify for persons with disabilities seeking representation in Bar Council committees?
x: The fee for persons with disabilities was set at ₹15,000, compared with ₹1.25 lakh otherwise.

s: Article 233 of the Constitution deals with the appointment of whom?
x: Article 233 concerns district judges; Articles 124 and 214 relate to the Supreme Court and High Courts.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Third Judges case – CJI and two senior judges
Judicial members of the NJAC – CJI plus four senior-most judges
NJAC case – 99th Amendment, 2014 struck down for violating the basic structure
Non-judicial members of the NJAC – CJI and two senior judges
x: The NJAC case struck down the 99th Amendment, 2014 for violating the basic structure. The Third Judges case set the collegium as CJI plus four senior-most judges; NJAC's judicial members were the CJI and two senior judges, and its non-judicial members the Law Minister and two eminent persons.

s: Which one of the following is correct about the Collegium system?
o: It is expressly provided in the Constitution.
It is not mentioned in the Constitution and emerged through the Three Judges Cases.
It was established by an Act of Parliament in 1998.
It was created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment.
x: The Collegium is not expressly provided in the Constitution; it evolved through the Three Judges Cases, including the 1998 judgment. The 99th Amendment created the NJAC, which was struck down in 2015.

s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was struck down in 2015 in which case?
x: The Fourth Judges (NJAC) Case of 2015 struck down the NJAC for violating judicial independence, part of the basic structure.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)?
o: Any two members could veto a name.
The Union Law Minister was a member.
It was chaired by the Union Law Minister.
x: The CJI chaired the NJAC; the Law Minister was only a member alongside two senior-most judges and two eminent persons.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for free legal aid and equal justice?
x: Article 39A provides for free legal aid and equal justice; Nyaya Setu builds on it.

s: According to the Supreme Court bench of Justice B. V. Nagarathna and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, Article 32 can be invoked only for which purpose?
o: Violation of any ordinary legal right
x: The Supreme Court bench held that Article 32 is meant only for violations of fundamental rights. The tempting broader option is incorrect because the Court specifically limited Article 32 to fundamental-rights violations.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed regional benches of the Supreme Court?
o: Constitutional matters would remain with the New Delhi bench.
The proposal seeks to address pendency of more than 90,000 cases (January 2026).
It was proposed through a private member Bill moved by P. Wilson.
Benches are proposed at Kolkata, Mumbai and Hyderabad besides New Delhi.
x: The proposed benches are at New Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai and Chennai, not Hyderabad; the other statements are correct.

s: Nyaya Setu, an AI chatbot providing free primary legal advice and linked to Tele-Law, was launched by which organisation?
o: Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa
x: Nyaya Setu is run by the Ministry of Law and Justice. It was first launched in August 2024 and its AI chatbot form, giving free primary legal advice and linked to Tele-Law, came on 1 January 2026.

s: Who virtually inaugurated India’s first fully paperless district court on 6 January 2026?
x: CJI Surya Kant virtually inaugurated India’s first fully paperless district court at Kalpetta in Wayanad, Kerala. Justice B. V. Nagarathna and Justice Ujjal Bhuyan were associated with the Article 32 matter, while Arjun Ram Meghwal gave the Rajya Sabha information on judges.

s: What was the focus of the India–Bhutan Supreme Courts MoU announced in January 2026?
o: Exchange of retired High Court judges as ad hoc judges
A 30% quota for women in Bar Council elections
Integration of the two countries' population registers
x: The India–Bhutan Supreme Courts MoU (January 2026) is for the exchange of young legal professionals. It does not deal with ad hoc judges, Bar Council quotas or population registers.

s: In 1987 the Law Commission recommended how many judges per 10 lakh population?
x: The Law Commission recommended 50; the Government reported only 22 per 10 lakh on the 2011 Census base.

s: Which institution developed the technology used in India’s first fully paperless district court at Kalpetta?
x: The technology was developed by the Kerala High Court and uses indigenous artificial-intelligence tools under the e-Courts project. The Supreme Court and Law Commission were not identified as the developers.

s: Which of the following pairs of Article and provision is correctly matched?
o: Article 217 – Acting Chief Justice of India
Article 126 – Retired judges sitting in the Supreme Court
Article 127 – Ad hoc Supreme Court judges
Article 128 – Appointment of High Court judges
x: Article 127 provides for ad hoc Supreme Court judges. Article 217 covers appointment of High Court judges, Article 126 the Acting CJI and Article 128 retired judges sitting in the Supreme Court.

s: Judicial independence was recognised as part of the basic structure in which case of 1973?
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) recognised judicial independence as part of the basic structure.

s: Who described Article 32 as the “heart and soul of the Constitution”?
x: B. R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the “heart and soul of the Constitution.” The other names are associated with the Supreme Court judiciary but were not the source of this description.

s: Why did Chief Justice of India Surya Kant call for a National Judicial Policy?
o: To replace the National Judicial Appointments Commission
To remove the requirement of consultation for High Court appointments
To place the Prime Minister’s election beyond judicial review
x: CJI Surya Kant called for a National Judicial Policy to reduce divergence across courts. The other options concern the NJAC or constitutional provisions and do not state the purpose of the proposed policy.

s: Under the Third Judges Case (1998), the collegium consists of the CJI and how many senior-most judges?
x: The Third Judges Case set the collegium as the CJI plus the four senior-most judges; the Second created the collegium.

s: The NJAC, struck down in 2015, was created by which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The 99th Amendment, 2014 created the NJAC; it was struck down for violating judicial independence.

s: When was Nyaya Setu, which gives free legal services on WhatsApp, first launched?
x: Nyaya Setu was first launched in August 2024; its AI chatbot form came on 1 January 2026.

s: Which of the following pairs of Judges Case and outcome is correctly matched?
o: Fourth Judges (2015) – Collegium of CJI and four judges
x: The First Judges Case gave executive primacy; the Second created the collegium, the Third set CJI + 4, and the Fourth struck down the NJAC.

s: Under Article 130, who may decide, with the President's approval, that the Supreme Court will sit at a place other than Delhi?
x: Article 130 makes Delhi the seat of the SC, but the CJI may, with the President's approval, decide other places.

s: How many members did the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) have?
x: The NJAC had six members: the CJI, two senior-most SC judges, the Union Law Minister and two eminent persons; any two could veto a name.

s: Where is India's first fully paperless district court, inaugurated in January 2026?
x: CJI Surya Kant virtually inaugurated the first fully paperless district court at Kalpetta, Wayanad, on 6 January 2026.

s: According to the Law Ministry's reply to the Rajya Sabha, India has about how many judges per 10 lakh population?
x: MoS Arjun Ram Meghwal told the Rajya Sabha there are 22 judges per 10 lakh; the Law Commission (1987) recommended 50.

s: The Committee of Privileges of the Lok Sabha has how many members?
x: The Lok Sabha committee has 15 members and the Rajya Sabha committee 10.

s: Which judgment overruled the JMM bribery (P.V. Narasimha Rao) case and held that bribery is not protected by legislative privilege?
o: Sita Soren v. Union of India
State of Kerala v. K. Ajith
M.S.M. Sharma v. Sri Krishna Sinha
x: Sita Soren (2024) overruled the 1998 JMM case, so bribes linked to speech or vote are not immune.

s:
Assertion (A): Parliamentary privileges continue to be based on the privileges of the British House of Commons as on 26 January 1950.
Reason (R): No law defining these privileges has been enacted yet.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true. Article 105(3) provides that, until privileges are defined by law, they remain those of the British House of Commons as on 26 January 1950; this continuing position follows because no defining law has yet been enacted.

s: Freedom from arrest in civil cases applies to legislators during a session and how many days before and after it?
x: Under Section 135A of the CPC, legislators are free from civil arrest during a session and 40 days before and after it.

s: Parliamentary privileges extend to which of the following?
x: Privileges extend to the Attorney General, not the President.

s: The Committee of Privileges of the Rajya Sabha has how many members?
x: The Rajya Sabha committee has 10 members and the Lok Sabha committee 15; both are semi-judicial.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about parliamentary privileges?
o: Under Article 105(3) they follow the British House of Commons as on 26 January 1950.
No law defining them has been enacted.
The Committee of Privileges is a judicial body.
The 44th Amendment protects fair press reporting of proceedings.
x: The Committee of Privileges is semi-judicial, not judicial; the other statements are correct.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Lok Sabha Privileges Committee is incorrect?
o: The Privileges Committee is a judicial body.
The Lok Sabha Privileges and Ethics Committees were not constituted for nearly two years.
Parliamentary privileges are provided under Article 105, while state legislative privileges are provided under Article 194.
The Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members.
x: The incorrect statement is that the Privileges Committee is a judicial body; it is described as semi-judicial. The other statements correctly reflect the non-constitution of the committees, Articles 105 and 194, and the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha.

s: In which case (1958) did the Supreme Court hold that legislative privileges under Article 194(3) prevail over freedom of the press?
o: M.S.M. Sharma v Sri Krishna Sinha (Searchlight case)
Sita Soren v Union of India
State of Kerala v K. Ajith
x: In the Searchlight case (M.S.M. Sharma v Sri Krishna Sinha, 1958) privileges were held to prevail over press freedom.

s: In which case (2021) did the Supreme Court hold that legislative privileges do not override criminal law?
o: State of Kerala v. K. Ajith
Sita Soren v. Union of India
x: State of Kerala v. K. Ajith (2021), on vandalism in the Kerala Assembly, held that privileges do not override criminal law.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment protected fair press reporting of the proceedings of Parliament (except secret sittings)?
x: The 44th Amendment (1978) protects fair press reports of parliamentary proceedings, except secret sittings.

s: Who is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, as noted in the 2026 privileges context?
x: The Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

s: What is the position of the Lok Sabha Speaker while a resolution for his removal is pending?
o: may preside and exercise a casting vote
cannot preside, but may speak and vote in the first instance
x: Under Article 96 the Speaker does not preside but may speak and vote in the first instance; there is no casting vote.

s: Notice of a resolution to remove the Lok Sabha Speaker must be given to the Secretary-General at least how many days in advance?
x: At least 14 days' written notice is needed, and at least 50 members must support leave.

s: In the notice moved against Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, which combination represented the Opposition's stated grievances?
o: The Opposition was not allowed to speak on the President's address, and eight MPs were suspended
Rahul Gandhi was not allowed to quote General M. M. Naravane's unpublished memoir, and the Speaker remarked that the Prime Minister could have been attacked in the House
The Speaker refused to allow discussion within 10 days, and did not permit 50 members to support the motion
The Speaker continued to preside while a removal resolution was pending, and exercised a casting vote
x: The notice cited LoP Rahul Gandhi not being allowed to quote Gen M.M. Naravane's unpublished memoir and the Speaker's remark that the PM could have been attacked in the House. The options on 10 days, 50 members, presiding and a casting vote describe the removal procedure, not the grievances.

s: Under Article 94(c), how must a resolution for removal of the Lok Sabha Speaker be passed?
o: By a unanimous vote of all members
By a majority of members present and voting
By a two-thirds majority of members present and voting
By a majority of all the then members of the House
x: Article 94(c) requires a majority of all the then members, commonly described as an effective majority. It is not a majority of members merely present and voting.

s: Which of the following pairs of Article and subject is correctly matched?
o: Article 93 – Vacation, resignation and removal of Speaker
Article 95 – Deputy Speaker acts as Speaker
Article 94 – Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
Article 96 – Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker
x: Article 95 lets the Deputy Speaker act as Speaker. Article 93 covers election, Article 94 vacation/resignation/removal, and Article 96 bars the Speaker from presiding while a removal resolution is pending.

s: Which of the following cases concerning the Speaker is NOT correctly matched?
o: Subhash Desai (2023) – Speaker should set timelines
Nabam Rebia (2016) – Speaker cannot decide disqualification while a removal notice is pending
Keisham Meghachandra Singh (2020) – Disqualification pleas should be decided within three months
Kihoto Hollohan (1993) – Disqualification pleas should be decided within three months
x: Kihoto Hollohan held that the Speaker's Tenth Schedule decisions are subject to judicial review; the three-month period is from Keisham Meghachandra Singh.

s: Against whom was the first motion to remove a Lok Sabha Speaker moved in 1954?
x: The 1954 motion was against G.V. Mavalankar, the first Speaker; motions against Hukam Singh (1966) and Balram Jakhar (1987) also failed.

s: Which case held that a Speaker cannot decide disqualification petitions while a notice for his removal is pending?
x: Nabam Rebia (2016) held so; Kihoto Hollohan made Tenth Schedule decisions reviewable and Subhash Desai asked the Speaker to set timelines.

s: Against which Lok Sabha Speaker was a removal motion moved in 1987?
x: Removal motions were moved against G.V. Mavalankar (1954), Hukam Singh (1966) and Balram Jakhar (1987); none succeeded.

s: Under which Article can the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly be removed?
x: Article 179 (like Article 94 for the Lok Sabha) deals with vacation, resignation and removal of the Assembly Speaker.
